, Reason for Mistake: The user’s initial “working hypothesis” chose C) erosion of rock debris as the most likely mechanism forming plateaus, conflating erosion (which primarily dissects and modifies uplifted surfaces) with the primary formation of plateaus. Plateaus generally originate from tectonic uplift or extensive basaltic lava flows; erosion then carves/dissects them. Among the listed options, lava flows are a true formative agent, while river runoff and wave weathering are not. This initial misclassification set the trajectory and was not corrected later, despite surfaced evidence (e.g., Britannica noting origins lie in tectonic processes and that erosion shapes landforms).
